As the Chief Product Officer, I've reviewed the customer's task for creating a Tetris game. Let me share my analysis on the product modality:

The core requirements here are: real-time falling tetrominoes, player interaction (moving/rotating pieces), dynamic board updates, line clearing with scoring, game-over logic, and progressive speed increase. These are all characteristics of an **interactive, visualized game** that demands continuous user input handling and real-time rendering.

Given these needs, I believe the most suitable modality is **Application** — it can implement the visualized game via Python (e.g., with Pygame), fully supporting keyboard controls, smooth animation of falling pieces, score display, and game state management. Other modalities like Website could theoretically host an HTML/JS version, but Application is our established and reliable format for games, ensuring all gameplay mechanics (seven tetromino shapes, rotation, line clears, speed progression) are realized robustly.

What's your opinion on this?
